subject: chemistry
title: Group 1 and Group 7
welcome_lead: Meet the soft fizzing metals and the colourful biting non-metals.
meta_desc: Explore alkali metals and halogens in this KS3 chemistry adventure on the periodic table.
final_note: You can now spot the highly reactive elements at the edges of the table.

concepts.def: Soft, reactive metals that fizz in water.
Group 1 gets MORE reactive going DOWN.
Group 7 gets LESS reactive going DOWN.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Group 1 contains lithium, sodium, potassium and more. They are soft enough to cut with a knife and react vigorously with water to make an alkali solution and hydrogen gas.

Reactivity increases going DOWN the group.

Group 7 contains fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine. They are coloured non-metals: F is pale yellow gas, Cl is green gas, Br is red-brown liquid, I is dark grey solid.

Reactivity decreases going DOWN the group.

Elements in the same group behave similarly because they have the same number of outer electrons.

Same group = same chemistry.
